STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a stainless mixing bowl of this look is typically a serving or salad bowl, roughly 20-25 cm.
b) Reference object: the kidney beans (or similar dark beans) are about 2.2-2.5 cm long. The bowl's visible inner diameter spans roughly 9-10 bean lengths across the rim area, giving about 22 cm.
Reconciled width: 22 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Countable pieces: I count about 14 visible dark red beans (kidney beans, likely cooked). Some are hidden under the pile; the cluster is only about one layer deep, so add about 3 hidden. Total ≈ 17 beans.
- Bean weight: a cooked kidney bean is about 1.2-1.5 g each in the 2.2 cm size class. Use 1.5 g. 17 x 1.5 = 26 g.
- Alternative check by volume: capacity = 0.2 x 22^3 / 1000 = 2.13 L (shallow). Visible fill is low, about 0.1 of the capacity by the surface footprint, so the volume is roughly 0.1 x 2.13 L ≈ 0.2 L... this is inconsistent with the piece count, so I trust the count: the beans occupy a sparse cluster, so the bowl is nearly empty. Taking ~26 g as the estimate is reasonable.
- Liquid or sauce: none visible, so none added.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible; the bowl bottom is bare metal, so no hidden base.

STEP 5 - kcal: cooked kidney beans ≈ 127 kcal per 100 g.

Total ≈ 26 g, about 33 kcal.
